headline: A 2020 law requires federal leasing agencies to check and disclose foreign ownership of landlords who lease high-security office space to the government.
what_it_does: Before the government signs or approves a lease for high-security office space, the landlord must name its top-level owner and say whether that owner is a foreign person or entity, including the country. Landlords must provide this when they first bid on a solicitation and update it every year. The General Services Administration must also create a government-wide plan for identifying owners of high-security leased spaces before leasing space to a federal tenant. The law also sets a rule for lease language that restricts access to high-security space.

who_it_affects.group: Companies and property owners that lease high-security office space to federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must disclose their highest-level owners, including whether any are foreign, when bidding and each year after.

who_it_affects.group: General Services Administration and other federal leasing agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must collect and review ownership disclosures and develop a government-wide plan for identifying owners of high-security leased spaces.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that occupy high-security leased space
who_it_affects.how: Leases for the space they use must follow the ownership disclosure process and the rule on access-restriction language.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 31, 2020; the specific effective dates for individual provisions are not stated in the summary provided.
